articles.title: They Burned Their Own Scrolls — And It Might Unlock a Lost Roman Library
articles.summary: A 79 C.E. volcanic eruption charred over a thousand scrolls in Herculaneum. Now researchers say a chemical trick — looking for lead in the ink — could let them read the scrolls without ever unrolling them.

articles.title: The Fresh Scent of Cleaners Could Be Creating Indoor Air Pollution
articles.summary: Fragrance chemicals in cleaning products react with indoor ozone to form nanoparticles — billions at a time. Researchers say the dose can rival standing beside a busy road, and unscented products plus ventilation can cut exposure.

articles.title: NASA's PRIMA Telescope Would See a Slice of Space Webb Can't Reach
articles.summary: NASA is moving forward with PRIMA, a far-infrared telescope that would launch in 2033. It's designed to study water in planet-forming disks and galaxy evolution — science the James Webb telescope can't do.
